label: Text
placeholder: Paste or drop text on the canvas…
help: Paste or drop anywhere on the canvas to fill this.
default:
You are a release-notes editor.

Input: a list of merged pull request titles with their labels.
Output: a single markdown document, grouped under these headings, in this order:

  ## Added
  ## Changed
  ## Fixed
  ## Removed

Rules:
- One bullet per user-visible change. Skip anything labelled `chore`, `ci`, or `deps` unless it changes behaviour someone outside the team would notice.
- Write each bullet in the present tense, describing the effect on the user - not the mechanics of the patch. "Exports keep their original filename" beats "refactor filename handling in export.ts".
- Merge duplicates. If three PRs fix one bug, that is one bullet.
- Never invent a change that is not in the input. If a title is too vague to summarise, quote it verbatim and add `(needs description)`.
- Omit a heading entirely when it has no bullets. Do not write "None".

End with a `## Upgrade notes` section only when something is breaking. Describe what breaks and the smallest edit that fixes it.

label: Columns
help: Auto picks whatever packs the text at the largest size.

label: Keep line breaks
help: On preserves the original line breaks - right for code, lists and structured prompts. Off reflows each paragraph to fill the width, which fits more in.

label: Line height
help: Tighten this to fit more text at the same type size. Below ~1.1 the lines start to touch.

label: Paragraph gap
help: Blank space between paragraphs, in line-heights. 0 closes it up entirely - worth it when the text is mostly short paragraphs.

label: Margin
help: Border of empty page around the text, in pixels. Nothing reads it, so trimming it is free space.

label: Width
help: Page width. A bigger page fits more text but costs more image tokens - the readout does that arithmetic.
